mainTopic: Heirs of a robber: יאוש, whether an heir is like a buyer, and רבא's reliance on רבי אושעיא's ברייתא
overview: The משנה teaches that if a robber fed stolen food to his children, or left a stolen item to them, they do not have to pay, unless it was 'something with אחריות.' רב חסדא rules that before יאוש, if a second person eats stolen food, the owner can collect from either person. When the משנה is raised as a challenge, the גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about after יאוש. רמי בר חמא learns from the משנה that an heir is like a buyer, so an inherited stolen item counts as having moved to a new owner. רבא disagrees: an heir is not like a buyer, and the משנה only exempts children who already ate the food. רבא reads 'something with אחריות' as land the father left. When רבי's teaching to his son contradicts that reading, רבא relies on the ברייתא of רבי אושעיא instead. The גמרא then tests that ברייתא against רב חסדא, who is defended with 'after יאוש,' and against רמי בר חמא, whose answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: a robber's children who ate or inherited stolen items
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that children who ate stolen food from their father, or inherited a stolen item, are exempt. But if the item 'has אחריות,' they must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone robs and feeds his children, or leaves the stolen item to them, they are exempt from paying. But if it was something that has אחריות, they must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the basic rule about a robber's children: usually they do not pay for what they ate or inherited, with one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two cases: the children ate the stolen food, or the father died and left the stolen item to them. In both cases they are exempt. The exception is property that 'has אחריות,' which the children must pay for.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'
One who robs (takes openly by force)
Exempt from paying
Property that can back up a debt (a guarantee)
Obligated

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who robs and feeds it to his children,
or left it before them (as an inheritance) —
they are exempt from paying.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיָה דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת –
phrases.english: But if it was something that has a guarantee (אחריות) —
phrases.notes: This means property that can back a loan. The גמרא explains exactly what it means later.

phrases.english: they are obligated to pay.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A robber's children who ate stolen food or inherited a stolen item are exempt, unless the item 'has אחריות.'

steps.title: רב חסדא: before the owner gives up hope, he can collect from either robber
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that if a robber's stolen item is eaten by a second person before the owner's יאוש, the owner may collect from whichever one he wants, because the item still belongs to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב חסדא said: If someone robbed, and the owners had not yet given up hope, and another person came and ate it from him, the owner may collect from this one or from that one. Why? As long as the owners have not given up hope, the item stays in its owner's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב חסדא about a second person who eats stolen food before the owner gives up hope, and explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יאוש, the item still legally belongs to the original owner. So the second person who ate it was really eating the owner's food, and he must pay. The first robber still owes too, because he was already obligated to return it, so the owner can choose whom to collect from.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא, the discussion on the משנה
The owners gave up hope of getting it back
Collects payment
What is the reason?
It stands in its owner's possession

steps.whyThisMatters: The line between before יאוש and after יאוש is the key to the whole סוגיא. The next two steps depend on it.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Chisda said:
If one robbed and the owners did not give up hope,
and another came and ate it from him —
if he wants, he collects from this one,
phrases.notes: The owner can collect from the first robber.

phrases.english: if he wants, he collects from that one.
What is the reason?
As long as the owners have not given up hope —
it stands in the possession of its owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: גָּזַל וְלֹא נִתְיָיאֲשׁוּ הַבְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a related rule about someone who eats stolen food from a robber.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before יאוש, the owner may collect from either the robber or the person who ate the item from him, because the item is still the owner's.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: the children who ate are exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה: children who ate their father's stolen food are exempt. That seems to go against רב חסדא, who makes the second eater pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: One who robs and feeds his children, or left it before them, they are exempt from paying. This is a refutation of רב חסדא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא using our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children are like the 'other person' in רב חסדא's case: they ate food that someone else stole. רב חסדא says such a person pays, but the משנה says the children are exempt. So the two seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
A strong refutation

phrases.english: We learned: One who robs and feeds his children,
or left it before them —
they are exempt from paying.
A refutation of Rav Chisda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's ruling from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that someone who eats from a robber must pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The children ate stolen food just like the 'other person,' yet the משנה exempts them.

steps.title: Answer: the משנה is after the owner gave up hope
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא can answer that the משנה is talking about after יאוש, while his own ruling is about before יאוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא can tell you: When that משנה was taught, it was about after יאוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא by saying the משנה and רב חסדא are talking about different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's whole reason was that before יאוש the item still belongs to the owner. After יאוש that reason is gone, so the children who ate can be exempt. The contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: He can tell you (a defense on someone's behalf)
After the owner gave up hope

steps.whatToRemember: Before יאוש: the owner can collect from either the robber or the one who ate it from him (רב חסדא). After יאוש: the robber's children who ate it are exempt (our משנה).

phrases.english: Rav Chisda can tell you:
When that one was taught —
it was after the owner gave up hope.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב חִסְדָּא: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is set after יאוש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to exempt the children even before יאוש, which would contradict רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is after יאוש, and רב חסדא is before יאוש, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: an heir is treated like a buyer
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's ruling that children who inherit a stolen item are exempt, רמי בר חמא learns that an heir's domain counts like a buyer's domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he left it before them, they are exempt from paying.' רמי בר חמא said: This tells us that the domain of an heir is like the domain of a buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the second case in the משנה (inheritance), and רמי בר חמא draws a general rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer who gets a stolen item after יאוש keeps it, because it has moved into a new person's domain. By exempting heirs, the משנה shows that inheriting also counts as moving into a new domain. The heir is not just a continuation of his father.

keyTerms.meaning: This tells us (a rule learned from the source)
The domain of an heir
The domain of a buyer
Is comparable

steps.confusionAlert: רמי בר חמא is not saying an heir is a buyer. He is saying the heir's domain is treated the same way for this law: the item counts as having moved to a new owner.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic question for the rest of the סוגיא: is an heir a new owner, or does he simply stand in his father's place?

phrases.english: If he left it before them —
they are exempt from paying.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא, זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת:
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said: This tells us:
the domain of an heir is like the domain of a buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא, זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the משנה's inheritance case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An heir's domain is like a buyer's domain: inheriting counts as the item moving to a new owner.

steps.title: רבא: an heir is not like a buyer
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רמי בר חמא. An heir's domain is not like a buyer's domain, so the משנה's exemption must be talking about children who already ate the stolen food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The domain of an heir is not like the domain of a buyer. And what case is the משנה dealing with? A case where they ate the stolen food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite opinion to רמי בר חמא: inheriting a stolen item does not make it the heir's, so the heir must return it. He then explains that the משנה exempts the children only because they already ate the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רמי בר חמא, the item passing to the heir works like a sale and changes ownership, so the heir keeps it. For רבא, the heir simply steps into his father's shoes, and the item still has to go back. That forces רבא to read the משנה's 'exempt' as a case where nothing is left to return.

keyTerms.meaning: The domain (ownership) of an heir
The domain (ownership) of a buyer
Is not comparable to
When they ate them (the stolen food)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא and רמי בר חמא are not arguing about what the משנה says. They are arguing about what it means: is the heir exempt because the item became his, or only because it is gone?

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: רְשׁוּת יוֹרֵשׁ לָאו כִּרְשׁוּת לוֹקֵחַ דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: The domain of an heir is not like the domain of a buyer,
and here, what case are we dealing with?
When they ate them.
phrases.notes: He means the children already ate the stolen food, so there is nothing left to give back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: רְשׁוּת יוֹרֵשׁ לָאו כִּרְשׁוּת לוֹקֵחַ דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רמי בר חמא's reading in step 5 and offers a different explanation of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An heir's domain is not like a buyer's domain, and the משנה's exemption refers to children who already consumed the stolen food.

steps.title: The end of the משנה shows the item still exists
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says that if the item has אחריות the children must pay. That implies the רישא is also about an item that still exists, which goes against רבא's 'they ate it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the latter clause teaches, 'If it was something that has אחריות, they must pay,' that implies the first clause is dealing with a stolen item that still exists!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא from the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא sets up a contrast: an item with אחריות must be paid for. A contrast only makes sense if the רישא is also about an item that is still there, just one without אחריות. If the רישא were about food already eaten, the סיפא's case would not be a matching contrast. So the רישא seems to exempt the heirs even when the stolen item exists, which is רמי בר חמא's view and not רבא's.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause (the end of the משנה)
The first clause (the beginning of the משנה)
A legal guarantee; property that stands behind a debt
It can be inferred that
A stolen item that still exists

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת –
phrases.english: If it was something that has a guarantee,
they are obligated to pay,
it can be inferred that in the first clause
we are dealing with a stolen item that still exists!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's reading of the משנה from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the משנה's exemption is about food that was already eaten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא's case of an item with אחריות implies, by contrast, that the רישא is about an existing item, so the exemption applies even when the item exists.

steps.title: רבא rereads the סיפא as talking about land
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the סיפא means: if the father left the children land (נכסים שיש להם אחריות), they must pay from it, even though the stolen food is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could answer you: This is what the משנה means. If their father left them land, they are obligated to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers by reading 'something with אחריות' as the father's land, not as the stolen item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the סיפא is no longer about the stolen object at all. The whole משנה is about food already eaten. If there is no other property, the children are exempt. If the father left land, the father's debt can be collected from it, so they must pay. This way there is no proof that the רישא is about an existing item.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)
This is what it means
Guaranteed property, meaning land

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:
This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הִנִּיחַ לָהֶם אֲבִיהֶם אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים,
phrases.english: If their father left them guaranteed property,
phrases.notes: Guaranteed property means land, which a creditor can always collect from.

phrases.english: they are obligated to pay.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Something with אחריות' refers to the stolen item itself, so the רישא is about an existing item.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Something with אחריות' refers to land the father left, so the whole משנה can be about stolen food that was eaten.

steps.title: רבי's teaching says it means a cow or donkey
steps.stepSummary: רבי taught his son that 'something with אחריות' is not literally land. It even includes a well-known cow or donkey, which the children return out of respect for their father. That goes against רבא's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי teach רבי שמעון his son: not something that literally has אחריות; rather even a cow he plows with, or a donkey he drives from behind, the children must return because of their father's honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer with a teaching from רבי, the editor of the משנה himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, the סיפא is about a recognizable stolen animal that still exists, not about land. The children return it so people won't point at it and shame their father as a thief. That brings back the problem: the סיפא is about an existing item, so the רישא must be too.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught him (how to learn the משנה)
Literally, actually
Drives a donkey (walking behind it)
Their father's honor

phrases.english: But didn't רבי teach
to רבי שמעון his son:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת מַמָּשׁ;
phrases.english: Not something that literally has a guarantee;
rather, even a cow that he plows with,
or a donkey that he drives from behind,
phrases.notes: These are animals everyone sees him using, so people would know they were his father's stolen goods.

phrases.english: they are obligated to return,
because of the honor of their father.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרֵיהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that 'something with אחריות' means land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי himself explained the phrase as a recognizable existing item, like a cow or donkey, which shows the משנה is about existing stolen items.

steps.title: רבא follows רבי אושעיא's reading
steps.stepSummary: רבא admits his reading does not match רבי's teaching. Instead he relies on רבי אושעיא, and says רבי אושעיא will come out to greet him in the next world for explaining the משנה his way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: When I die, רבי אושעיא will come out toward me, because I explain our משנה like him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא keeps his view, but now openly bases his reading of the משנה on רבי אושעיא instead of רבי. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not try to fit his reading into רבי's teaching. He accepts that it disagrees, and points out that there is another תנא, רבי אושעיא, who learned the משנה the way he does. Following that tradition honors רבי אושעיא, so he will welcome רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: When I die
Will come out toward me (to greet me)
I explain

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
When I die,
רבי אושעיא will come out toward me,
phrases.notes: He means רבי אושעיא will greet him in the next world as a way of honoring him.

phrases.english: because I explain our משנה according to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by relying on a different תנא's version of the teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relying on a different tradition (רבי אושעיא instead of רבי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's reading must fit רבי's explanation of the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא follows רבי אושעיא's tradition, which supports his reading even though it differs from רבי's.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא's ברייתא matches רבא exactly
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא's ברייתא says: children who ate stolen food are exempt. An inherited stolen item that still exists must be returned, and one that is gone does not. If the father left land, they must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי אושעיא taught: One who robs and feeds his children, they are exempt from paying. If he left it to them: if the stolen item exists, they are obligated; if it does not exist, they are exempt. If their father left them land, they are obligated to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא of רבי אושעיא that רבא relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every piece fits רבא. An existing inherited item must be returned, so the heir is not like a buyer. Eaten or lost items are exempt, which is how רבא read the רישא. Land left by the father makes them pay, which is exactly how רבא read the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught (introduces a ברייתא)
One who robs
Left it before them (as an inheritance)
Exempt

steps.whatToRemember: רבא holds an heir is not like a buyer: an existing inherited stolen item goes back. He reads the משנה like רבי אושעיא. The exemption is for food already eaten, and 'something with אחריות' means land the father left. רבי's teaching to his son reads the משנה differently.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives רבא an early source, a ברייתא of רבי אושעיא, for his reading of the משנה, even though רבי's teaching to his son reads it differently. The next steps test this same ברייתא against both רב חסדא and רמי בר חמא.

phrases.english: For רבי אושעיא taught:
One who robs and feeds it to his children,
they are exempt from paying.
If he left it to them,
if the stolen item still exists, they are obligated;
if the stolen item does not exist, they are exempt.
If their father left them guaranteed property,
they are obligated to pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that רבא said he follows in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that an heir is not like a buyer, and his reading of the משנה (eaten food; land for אחריות).

steps.title: The ברייתא's exemption seems to go against רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ruling that heirs are exempt if the stolen item is gone. It asks whether this disproves רב חסדא, who holds that people who eat stolen food can be made to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: if the stolen item no longer exists, the heirs are exempt. Shall we say this is a refutation of רב חסדא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes one line from רבי אושעיא's ברייתא. Then it asks whether that line disproves the view of רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא holds that when someone else eats stolen food, the owner can collect from the person who ate it. The heirs here ate the food, yet the ברייתא says they are exempt. That looks like a direct contradiction of רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' A formula for quoting a line from a source that was just cited, so the גמרא can analyze it.
Still exists, still intact.
Exempt, they do not have to pay.
A refutation, a strong challenge that could knock down an opinion.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Let us say' (נימא) does not mean the גמרא has concluded that רב חסדא is wrong. It is only raising the possibility, and the next step defends him.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This means the ברייתא of רבי אושעיא that was just quoted in Step 11.

phrases.english: If the stolen item no longer exists, they are exempt.
Shall we say this is a refutation of רב חסדא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא brought as support in Step 11 and tests one of its rulings against another אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that whoever eats stolen food can be made to pay.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The heirs ate the stolen food, yet the ברייתא exempts them. That contradicts רב חסדא.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the ברייתא is about a case after the owners gave up hope
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case after the owners gave up hope (יאוש). His own ruling is about a case before יאוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא could tell you: that ברייתא is taught about a case after the owners gave up hope.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא by limiting the ברייתא to a different case than the one he was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the owners have given up hope, the heirs who ate the food are exempt, just as the ברייתא says. רב חסדא only obligated the eater before יאוש. So the two rulings deal with different cases and do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He could say to you.' This introduces a defense on behalf of the person being challenged.
'When that ברייתא was taught.' This introduces a limit on which case a source is talking about.
The owner giving up hope of ever getting the item back.

steps.whyThisMatters: יאוש is a turning point in the laws of stolen property. Whether the owners have given up hope can change who is responsible to pay.

phrases.english: רב חסדא could say to you:
When that ברייתא was taught, it was about a case after the owners gave up hope.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the ברייתא is about a case after יאוש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא exempts heirs who ate the stolen food in every case, which would contradict רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption applies only after יאוש. רב חסדא's ruling, which obligates the eater, is about a case before יאוש.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַב חִסְדָּא: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא – לְאַחַר יֵאוּשׁ

steps.title: The ברייתא's obligation seems to go against רמי בר חמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ruling that heirs must pay if the stolen item still exists. It asks whether this disproves רמי בר חמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: if the stolen item still exists, the heirs must pay. Shall we say this is a refutation of רמי בר חמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second line from the same ברייתא and tests it against another אמורא, רמי בר חמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא holds that when heirs inherit an item, it counts as passing into a new owner's hands, so they should not have to return it. The ברייתא says the heirs must pay when the item still exists. That looks like it contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: They are obligated to pay, here by returning the item.
'Shall we say?' This introduces a suggested conclusion that may be pushed away.

phrases.english: The Master said:
If the stolen item still exists, they are obligated to pay.

phrases.aramaic: נֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא?
phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of רמי בר חמא?

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the same pattern as Step 12, now testing a different line of the ברייתא against a different אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's view that inheriting an item counts as a change of ownership.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If inheriting is a change of ownership, the heirs should keep the item. Yet the ברייתא obligates them to pay.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא begins his answer by limiting the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא starts to answer, using the same pattern as רב חסדא: 'that ברייתא was taught about...'. The rest of his answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא could tell you: when that ברייתא was taught...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins defending רמי בר חמא. The amud ends in the middle of his sentence, so the actual answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'כי תניא ההיא' tells us he will defend himself the same way רב חסדא did. He will limit the ברייתא to a specific case where his rule does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose view on inheriting stolen property is being tested.

phrases.english: רמי בר חמא could say to you:
When that ברייתא was taught...
phrases.notes: The amud ends mid-sentence. The case he means is spelled out on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case. The specific case is given in the continuation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא obligates heirs in every case, which would contradict רמי בר חמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא will be limited to a specific case. That case is stated on the next amud.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא
